rustc_to_emcc: rustc passes its optimization level to emcc as -Os for opt-level "s" and -Oz for "z" (seen in the logged link line), and -g0 for no debug info. Its own -sEXPORTED_FUNCTIONS list (every exported symbol, the cxxbridge glue included) comes first; build.rs's -sEXPORTED_FUNCTIONS=_main,_ps_alloc,_ps_free,_ps_call comes later and wins. rustc adds -sABORTING_MALLOC=0 and -sWASM_BIGINT last. cc-rs compiles the shim with -Os or -Oz from the same profile.

breakdown_V0.attribution_method: a second link of V0 with -C link-arg=--profiling-funcs and -C link-arg=-Wl,-Map=<file> (cargo rustc, analysis only; its code section is 401 bytes larger than V0's and has the same 30,477 functions). Each function of the name section is attributed by the input file that wasm-ld's map gives for it: OCCT objects (bundled in libpartsmith_occt_sys's rlib) to their toolkit through the source files of each toolkit's PACKAGES, shim and cxx objects to the shim, Emscripten system libraries to the runtime, libc, libc++ and dlmalloc. Functions of the one Rust LTO object go to the first Partsmith crate their demangled (v0) name mentions, so std, serde and hashbrown code instantiated for a Partsmith type counts for that crate; else to the first other crate named. Only __wasm_call_ctors (15,366 bytes, the static constructors) is not in the map; it is counted as linker-generated.

notes_for_next_builder: cargo writes the Emscripten binary to wasm32-unknown-emscripten/wasm-release/deps/partsmith_core.wasm and .js with no hash in the file name, so opt-level s and z builds (different partsmith-wasm units) write the same two files, and a build cargo finds fresh copies out whatever the last link wrote. Every variant of this record was relinked (each emcc log holds its own link).
